function: Joint user selection (DQN), BS beamforming and RIS phase-shift control (DDPG) by multi-agent hierarchical DRL, maximizing long-term QoE under WiFi-interference and latency constraints (p. 6, 9).
system: Multi-antenna BSs (Nm=10), 12 single-antenna users each, one reflecting passive RIS per BS (L=20 elements, ideal unit-modulus); 5 GHz, 40 MHz (p. 4, 10).
method: Multi-agent hierarchical DRL (MAHDRL): DQN for user selection, DDPG for beams and RIS phases, QMIX-style mixing network; centralized training, distributed execution; reinforcement learning (p. 8-9).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rician fading (κ=1) with free-space path loss, BSs and RISs uniformly placed in 300x300 m2, Poisson traffic; no dataset or measurement (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: No train/test split stated; reward over 400 episodes (Fig. 3); sweeps of users 11-20, WiFi APs 2-20, RIS elements 4-40, Rmin 3/5 Mbps (p. 11-12).
baselines: Learned only: MADDPG (discrete actions relaxed), CC-MAHDRL (centralized-critic hierarchical DQN+MADDPG), MAHDRL without RIS (ablation); no classical or non-learned baseline (p. 11).
metrics: Reward (QoE-based), average data rate per BS and per user, user latency, WiFi received interference, user reliability, convergence over episodes (p. 11-12).
complexity: Analytical order of complexity, Eq. (43): M times the layer-wise FCNN costs of the DQN, actor, and critic networks; no runtime or parameter count (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "Rician factor κ is chosen from the interval" - custom Rician fading with free-space path loss (Table I, p. 10: Rician factor κ = 1); no 3GPP model, ray-tracing dataset, or measurement is used or mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "Fig.4 shows the impact of the Metaverse user number Km" - only sweeps over users, WiFi APs and RIS elements (pp. 11-12); the paper never says a trained model is tested in a setting unseen in training, and the network input sizes scale with Km (p. 10: I0 = 3Km), so no transfer is shown.
q3_support: p. 11: "MAHDRL without RIS: The proposed architecture" - the three benchmarks (MAHDRL without RIS, MADDPG, CC-MAHDRL) are all learned, and MAHDRL without RIS is an ablation of the proposed method; no optimization, random or fixed-configuration non-learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "complexity of the proposed MAHDRL algorithm can be" - written as O(M(...)(...)(...)) in Eq. (43), from the layer sizes of the DQN, actor and critic networks (Section IV-C).
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider a RIS-assisted NR-U network with BSs and" - custom simulation set-up (Table I); no code or data link, no public dataset or measured data; code release is not mentioned anywhere.
notes: Included: the learned MAHDRL decides user selection (DQN) jointly with BS beams and RIS phase shifts (DDPG), so above_phy does not apply (pp. 6, 9); area 3. Title and DOI checked on p. 1 (JSAC vol. 42 no. 3, 2024). Table I read from the page image (p. 10).
